insight.title: Why Book Pages Have Wide Margins
insight.subtitle: How a medieval pest control trick shaped the layout of modern digital screens.
insight.notificationHook: Why book pages have blank margins

sections.text: Every time you open a book or a blank digital document, you see wide margins. They aren't there for aesthetics; they were originally designed as an ancient, physical defense system.

In medieval libraries, hungry mice and rats regularly chewed on the outer edges of expensive manuscripts. Scribes realized that by clustering text in the center, the rodents would only eat the blank parchment.

Though modern pest control eventually solved the rodent problem, our eyes became so accustomed to this protective frame that it became permanent—surviving all the way into the digital layout of our screens.
Your Google Docs are still formatted to outsmart medieval rats.
